title: Microsoft Teams: mandatory pre-meeting consent for meeting participants
summary: Hold: the route to Customize message skips enabling the consent toggle, which Microsoft's instructions require first. The page also infers that people who cannot see the message cannot join, although Microsoft does not document that outcome and lists join scenarios where consent does not apply.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams is adding mandatory pre-meeting consent configurable by tenant admins.
claims.quote: We are providing a new configuration experience in Teams Admin Center where tenant admins can enable and customize an explicit consent message before joining any meeting hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: Pre-meeting consent is governed by the meeting policy assigned to the organiser.
claims.quote: Pre-meeting consent is controlled through Teams meeting policies and is turned off by default. When enabled, the consent experience applies to meetings organized by users who are assigned the policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn feature page labels the feature Public Preview, unlike the roadmap and notice's General Availability phase.
claims.quote: This feature is currently in Public Preview.

claims.claim: The enable control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Enable pre-meeting participant consent.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Enable pre-meeting participant consent toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true enables the consent requirement.
claims.quote: $true: All participants must explicitly accept a custom consent dialog before joining any meeting hosted by the tenant. Note: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.
claims.fix: Keep the call, but add to the maturity paragraph: 'The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference also says EnablePreMeetingConsent and PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier have no effect because the feature is not fully released, while the feature guide documents using them.' Both pages are already cited.

claims.claim: Consent content must be configured and associated with the policy.
claims.quote: Requires at least one consent content entry configured in TeamsPreMeetingConsentConfiguration.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Admins reach Customize message directly through Meeting join & lobby without first enabling pre-meeting participant consent.
claims.quote: 3. Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Enable pre-meeting participant consent toggle On. 4. Select Customize message.
claims.fix: Replace the message path in front matter and table with 'Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Enable pre-meeting participant consent > Customize message'. Add to its note: 'Turn the consent toggle On before selecting Customize message.' Replace the first At rollout bullet with 'In the chosen policy, turn on Enable pre-meeting participant consent, select Customize message, compose the message and use Preview before saving.' This follows https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/pre-meeting-consent.

claims.claim: New-CsPreMeetingConsent -LocalizedContent <localized content> creates the consent message configuration.
claims.quote:
$consent = New-CsPreMeetingConsent `
    -LocalizedContent @(
        $englishContent
        $frenchContent
    )

claims.claim: The consent content is a separate configuration, assigned to a meeting policy by passing its returned identifier to Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier.
claims.quote:
Copy the configuration identifier returned by New-CsPreMeetingConsent:
$consentId = "<consent-configuration-guid>"
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy `
    -Identity $policyIdentity `
    -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier $consentId `
    -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true

claims.claim: Admins must remove content assignment from all meeting policies before deleting a consent configuration.
claims.quote: Before deleting a configuration, remove the content assignment from all meeting policies.

claims.where: Scope: Roles and prerequisites; Governance controls
claims.claim: The pre-meeting consent Learn page does not name a required admin role.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent admin role Teams Rooms PSTN bots audit event'; read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/pre-meeting-consent in full. It names admins but no specific required admin role.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page and supplied notice name no licence specific to pre-meeting consent.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent licensing license Teams Premium price meter'; read pre-meeting-consent and MC1454114 fully, Premium licensing excerpts and user-access. No feature-specific entitlement found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence requirement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' under the standard's product-level entitlement rule. Replace the licensing notes and corresponding prose with 'Teams requires a Teams license for each user in the organization, except anonymous meeting joins. A requirement specific to pre-meeting consent is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Retain cost low and the narrower unpublished feature-specific licensing caveat.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page and notice name no price or meter for pre-meeting consent.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent licensing license Teams Premium price meter'; opened pre-meeting-consent and user-access, read Premium licensing and add-on licensing excerpts and MC1454114. No price or meter for this feature found.

claims.claim: The Learn feature page describes no agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent admin role Teams Rooms PSTN bots audit event'; read pre-meeting-consent fully. It describes participant acknowledgement and admin configuration, not an agent or an automated action.

claims.claim: A participant who cannot see the consent message cannot join the meeting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent participants unsupported client cannot see consent message join'; read pre-meeting-consent and results. The guide documents declining consent and exempt join scenarios, not this unseen-message outcome.
claims.fix: Replace 'A participant who declines or cannot see the message cannot join' with 'A participant who declines the message cannot join'. Remove 'and from users on the mobile join paths above' from the helpdesk forecast: those paths are documented exceptions, not documented failed joins.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Changing an organiser's assigned meeting policy changes which pre-meeting consent setting applies to their meetings.
claims.quote: When enabled, the consent experience applies to meetings organized by users who are assigned the policy.

claims.claim: Admins can review Teams consent audit records in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: To retrieve audit logs for Teams activities, use the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Audit data is only visible in the audit log if auditing is turned on.
claims.fix: Remove the audit-review checklist bullet as requested by the table-consistency finding. If retaining its factual premise in Risk assessment: Data exposure, use 'Teams audit data is retrieved through Microsoft Purview and is visible only if auditing is turned on.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-teams-audit-log-events. Keep the specific consent activity name as an open question.

claims.claim: The pre-meeting consent Learn page does not explain how Teams Rooms, PSTN dial-in participants or meeting bots meet the requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams pre-meeting consent audit activity Purview Teams Rooms PSTN bots' and 'Teams pre-meeting consent admin role Teams Rooms PSTN bots audit event'; read pre-meeting-consent fully. Rooms, PSTN and bot handling is not stated there.

claims.claim: Participant agreement for recording and transcription is a different meeting policy option from pre-meeting consent.
claims.quote: Within your chosen policy, navigate to the Recording & Transcription section. Toggle the Require participant agreement for recording and transcription setting On or Off.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/participant-agreement-recording-transcription to sources for this distinction.
